title: Customer Onramp: Custom Pathways 90-Day Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook is a flexible onramp blueprint for midsize to enterprise customers adopting Redwood Inference. It emphasizes tailored pathways (technical-forward, executive-forward, and hybrid) and ties onboarding milestones directly to renewal triggers and health signals. Use as a living document during pre-sales handoffs and the first 90 days of engagement.

Core principles (how to use this doc):
- Start where the customer needs you: choose one pathway and map milestones to their top 3 outcomes.
- Instrument early: link each milestone to a measurable signal (metrics listed below) so we can automate health scoring.
- Keep a single owner but cross-functional execution: CSM owns outcomes, Solutions Engineer (SE) owns technical enablement, Account Exec (AE) stays engaged as renewal sentinel.
- Surface risks early and run weekly mini-experiments to reduce friction.

Audience: CSMs, Solutions Engineers, Onboarding PMs, Customer Success Ops.

Top-level outcome statements (pick up to three per customer):
- Deliver first production call with targeted latency and cost targets (example: p50 < 120ms, cost per 1k tokens <$8).
- Achieve 1st end-user-facing feature using Redwood API within 45 days.
- Demonstrate credible ROI with a customer usage dashboard and stakeholder exec review by day 75.

Success metrics (KPIs we will track):
- Time-to-first-meaningful-call (days)
- First-value event completion (e.g., first embed+search query, first chat flow sold to users)
- Weekly active integrations (number of unique endpoints hitting Redwood API weekly)
- Token volume ramp (tokens/day) and cost per 1k tokens trend
- Mean inference latency p50/p95 for production endpoints
- Health score composite (0-100): product usage, error rate, exec engagement, open blockers

Renewal triggers and early signals:
- Positive triggers: steady token growth > 15% month-over-month, exec monthly review scheduled, spike in user retention linked to feature using Redwood services.
- Risk signals: stalled implementation > 21 days on critical checklist item, repeated errors in top 3 endpoints, exec no-shows for >2 consecutive status meetings, declining token usage for 3 weeks.

Stakeholder matrix (example):
- CSM (owner) — success metrics, meeting cadence, renewals nudges.
- SE — API integration, sample prompts, perf diagnostics.
- Eng PM (customer) — roadmap alignment.
- Security/Compliance contact — private deployment/KMS milestones.
- Finance/Billing contact — invoicing, reserved capacity decisions.

90-day plan (pathway-agnostic template)
Phase 0: Pre-day-0 (handshake & prep, usually during procurement/contract)
- Owner: CSM + SE
- Key activities: kickoff scheduling, environment access request (API keys, VPC peering if private), sample data checklist, prioritized success outcomes captured in one-pager.
- Deliverables: Kickoff agenda, access matrix, initial runbook for SE (sample model, test prompt set).

Days 1–30: Build & Validate (momentum)
- Objectives: Complete environment setup, run first sandbox calls, validate latency and auth flows, onboard dev champion.
- Technical checklist:
  - Validate API key access and scopes.
  - Run sample inference tests (p50/p95 baseline captured).
  - Confirm model selection and initial parameter settings (temp, top_p, max_tokens).
  - Implement simple test harness or Postman collection for automated smoke tests.
- CS checklist:
  - Host kickoff (executive + tech split sections).
  - Schedule weekly standups with dev champion.
  - Collect 3 success use-cases and tie to metrics.
- Risk mitigation steps:
  - If smoke tests fail: open ticket in CS-ENG queue and schedule 1:1 triage within 48 hours.

Days 31–60: Expand & Stabilize (first-value)
- Objectives: Move from sandbox to staging, validate performance under expected load, build first end-to-end user flow.
- Technical checklist:
  - Integrate into staging environment, verify KV cache & batching config for target QPS.
  - Implement prefix caching for conversational flows where appropriate.
  - Begin monitoring: latency dashboards, error rates, token cost.
- CS checklist:
  - Run feature acceptance test with product owner.
  - Host walkthrough for internal stakeholders; capture feedback.
  - Start renewal-health conversations with AE: are we tracking expected usage?
- Experimentation prompts:
  - Test a quantized model variant vs baseline to compare cost/latency tradeoffs.

Days 61–90: Launch & Demonstrate Value (exec alignment)
- Objectives: Launch to production (limited or full), hold exec review showing ROI, finalize go-forward ops plan.
- Technical checklist:
  - Production rollout: canary or gradual ramp per Redwood Console rollout options.
  - Finalize autoscaling and burst policies for Dedicated customers.
  - Ensure alerting thresholds and runbooks for SRE/ops are in place.
- CS checklist:
  - Run executive demo with concrete metrics (tokens/day, p50 latency, cost delta).
  - Deliver adoption plan for next 90–180 days including optimization cadence.
  - Document success stories and internal case notes to pass to Customer Success Operations for QBR prep.

Handoff & Renewals play (post-90):
- Deliver a renewal readiness packet 45 days before contract renewal: trend lines, usage forecast, open blockers, roadmap asks.
- If renewal at risk: launch a fast-ops war room (CS lead + SE + AE + Eng PM) with 3-week sprint to resolve top blockers.

Tactical templates (copy-paste)
1) Week 1 kickoff agenda (60 mins)
- 0–5: Welcome + outcome alignment (CSM)
- 5–20: Business goals & success metrics (AE/CSM)
- 20–40: Technical runthrough: access, sample calls, security (SE)
- 40–55: Risks & dependencies (all)
- 55–60: Action items & owners (CSM)

2) Dev champion onboarding checklist (share as a Google Sheet)
- API keys provisioned
- Sample prompt set run and baseline results recorded
- Postman/smoke tests added to CI or dev harness
- Security review scheduled (if private)

3) Exec review slide bullets (10–12 mins)
- One-line value delivered (customer metric improved)
- Key metric trends: token ramp, latency p50/p95, cost trajectory
- Roadmap asks and recommended Redwood configurations (Dedicated/Private/Model quantization)
- Next steps and renewal ask timeline

Sample outreach templates (email snippets)
- Kickoff invite subject: "Redwood + <Customer> Kickoff — Align on 90-day outcomes"
- Post-kickoff follow-up: short numbered action items with owners and due dates (copyable into Jira)

Risk register example (quick triage table in doc)
- Missing infra access — impact: blocks phase 0 — mitigation: escalate to AE/Infra owner, target resolution <48h.
- Performance gaps at staging — impact: delays to production — mitigation: schedule SE perf deep-dive and run model quantization test within 7 days.

Operational notes for CSMs:
- Keep a living single-source-of-truth doc for each customer: include milestone dates, open tickets, and exec contact cadence.
- Tag every Jira ticket that relates to onboarding with prefix ONR-<customer initials> so CS Ops can generate dashboards.
- Use Redwood Console snapshots for screenshots in exec decks (p50/p95 charts, cost breakdowns).

Appendix: suggested automation and CS-Ops integrations
- Health score automation: pull weekly metrics from Console (tokens, p50, errors), exec meeting attendance, and open-blocker count -> composite health score.
- Renewal forecast rule: if health score < 60 and token ramp < 2% week-over-week for 4 weeks -> create 'renewal-risk' Slack channel and schedule AE+CSM escalation.

Notes & open questions (things to collect per customer during discovery):
- Which stakeholders own inference SLAs inside the customer org?
- What are their throughput expectations and peak concurrency?
- Any data residency or KMS needs that push for Private deployment?

Document history:
- 2026-02-20: created (initial draft)
- 2026-03-10: updated with renewal playbook & automation rules (this version)

Quick next steps for the CSM reading this today:
1) Pick the pathway most aligned to the customer's primary outcome (technical/exec/hybrid).
2) Fill the one-pager template with 3 outcomes and target dates before the kickoff.
3) Add ONR-<customer> tag to any related tickets and sync with SE for sample test plan.

End of playbook.
